reviews.review: One of the best 40k games out there. You need to play this!
Best game to purge greenskins in the name of the emperor

Here is a review from someone who played this game on both PS3 (on first release) and PC and who's a REAL big fan of the WH40K universe. which means: i love the lore-books, the tabletop games and the Dawn of War-series AND THIS GAME! (you'll read later on why i don't reccomend it)

The entire review in short:
if you want to play this game, play it for the singleplayer or the exterminatus, unless you feel like getting your ass handed to you in unfair multiplayer combat.
(giving this game a "no" on reccomendation is painfull to me, since i'm such a big fan of the Wh40K universe)

[b]Single Player & Story[/b]
Space marine is THQ's very brutal and gory take on the Warhammer 40K universe and it's story does not follow the official Lore but instead the people at THQ wrote their own story for this game (Glossing over all that official lore you don't really need to know):
Orks attack an Imperial Forge World for the joy of fighting and with the goal to loot the Titans [i](GIGANTIC walking, machines with ridiculously large weapons)[/i] garrissoned there. In response, the Imperium sends out the Ultramarines to whipe out the ork threat and secure the Titans. While an Inquisitor is working on an experimental weapon that uses pure warp-energies, but this is the cause of a WAY bigger threat.

[b]The game itself on the other hand.... (Gameplay)[/b]
- Fighting the ork hordes [i](Yes, massive hordes of green-skinned orks that come at you with near-unending numbers for you to fully purge, in the name of the Emperor!)[/i] with a space marine is awesome, brutal, bloody and gore galore! (unless you just go round stunning and executing orks, that way the game gets repetitive REAL QUICK, but that's how you play this game [b]wrong![/b])
THQ gives you a nice arsenal of WH40K weapons to deal with this sea of green violence, and 1 weapon they invented themselves: The Vengeance Launcher (not a fan of this weapon, it's clunky and requires too many buttons to work effectively in my opinion).
My favorite being the Chainsword (which is exactly what the name suggests: a sword with a motorised chainsaw build into it, roaring violently and bloodthirsty with each swing you take at the storming orks.)
Ofcourse the game gets even better than that:
Space Marines are genetically enhanced super soldiers, made by the God-Emperor himself to enforce his will and to keep the peace within his domain. This means: they are taller than your home's front door, stronger than John Cena and more buff than Arnould Schwartsenegger in his movie-prime and wear a power armor just as strong as a tank of today's age, and yet these orks are capable of killing these super soldiers with just scrap weapons and stolen guns (since they are incapable of building a proper technology of their own)
The Space Marines get more violent if they get wounded and THQ implemented this into their Singleplayer nicely: As you start playing this game you'll notice that the only thing you'll find on the ground is ammo, no healthpacks, because the enemies ARE YOUR WALKING HEALTHPACKS!!! if you get low on hp, you can always refill that Red bar of goodness by stunning an enemy and then executing him (in a very violent method that usually only leaves half of a mingled ork body on the floor and covers your shiney armor in thick-red ork blood)

[b]Ork Behaviour (AI programming) [/b]
After playing this game for so many years i noticed on a number of occasions that these orks use their (small) brains to get you, instead of just mindlessly running at you with their weapon above their heads.
Although these tactics are on the same level as a 6-year old child would come up with --> Some orks will turn around and hide themselves in a crack in the wall or wait around a corner to strike at you when you pass, if they notice that their numbers are running thin.
ALL orks also do efforts to dodge your shots (they already start running zig-zag when you aim your gun at them.
Shootah-boyz and -Nobs (Ork Ranged units) actively look for the high ground so they can shoot you better. (For a race that's too impatient to aim a gun by lore, they sure shoot damn straight... =/ ) They also make use of available cover.
(You on the other hand have your powerarmor, you don't need cover)

[b]The achievements[/b] in this game are unlike the achievements of other games and will keep you buisy for quite a while. Example: play an entire chapter (of choice) with just these 2 specific weapons. Or: Kill a total of 40.000 [i](yes, that many)[/i] enemies in both single and multiplayer.

MULTIPLAYER:
- THQ made an unbalanced multiplayer, after their bankrupcy, Sega took the game over and refused to fix ANY of this . . .
- Recently, certain people started to hack their loadout slots, allowing them to bring to the battlefield whatever overpowered combinations they feel like from any classes . . .
- Sega IS making Space Marine 2, BUT since they managed to ♥♥♥♥ up Dawn of War 3, i wouldn't get my hopes up, if I were you...
- This game offers some DLC. All of which are cosmetics, even the weapons (YES the powersword is actually just a normal chainsword, it hits just as fast and does just as much damage!!!)
[b]* DLC Gamemodes:[/b]
[b]Chaos Unleashed:[/b] new maps and 2 new gamemodes for multiplayer (nobody plays this, or you'll have to check out Chapter Master Valrak on youtube to get some dates where he plays this game with his subscribers)
Chaos Unleashed also offers new maps to play Exterminatus gamemode on, and you don't play as a space marine but as a Chaos Marine instead and the enemy now also switches its waves between orks and (new) Imperial Guard.
[b]Dreadnought Assault:[/b] A multiplayer gamemode (that nobody plays anyway) where you need to fight over and capture a single point on the map in order to instantly respawn as a Dreadnought (a large, walking machine with a one-hitting melee attack and 2 heavy bolters as a ranged weapon (yes, that hurts ingame!) to unleash complete devastation upon the battlefield)
IF you feel like playing one of these (underpopulated) DLC gamemodes, i suggest you play a lot of the populated gamemodes first, get to meet some of the friendlier folk on there and ask them if they want to play some DLC with you.
